sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Dharmendra Dwivedi, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri Somnath Seth, Advocate for respondent.

Order 
Petitioner has preferred this miscellaneous petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India seeking following reliefs:-
"(i) That, the impugned order dated 05.02.2024 (Annexure P/1) passed by the Learned 7th District Judge, Bhind in Civil Appeal No.79/2023 may kindly be set aside.
(ii) Any other suitable direction/relief which this Hon'ble Court deems fit in the facts and circumstances of the case also may kindly be passed.

(iii) Costs of present petition may also kindly be awarded to the petitioners."
2.

Brief facts of the case are that respondent/plaintiff filed a suit for the purpose of recovery of rent of Rs.2,88,000/- and for the arrears of rent which NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:21956 2 MP-941-2024 was valued at Rs.1,68,000/- and total suit valuation is Rs.4,56,000/- and Court fee of Rs.54,720/- was paid on the same.
Petitioner/defendant paid entire arrears of rent during pendency of the suit.
Suit has been decreed on the ground of bonafide need.

Petitioner has challenged the same by way of filing civil appeal only on the issue of bonafide need and not against arrears of rent and thus, she has valued the appeal at Rs.2,88,000/- and paid Court Smt Divya Shrivastava vs Baijnath Prasad on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104930264/
1 fee of Rs.24,000/- but same was not considered by First Appellate Court and directed the petitioner to pay requisite Court fee of Rs.30,720/-.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid, petitioner has preferred this petition.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the Trial Court has exercised its jurisdiction contrary to law.
She has already paid Court fee on the relief sought.
She did not seek any relief regarding arrears of rent and properly valued her appeal, but same was ignored by the First Appellate Court.

Hence, she prays that the impugned order dated 05.02.2024 (Annexure P-1)
passed by Seventh District Judge, Bhind in Civil Appeal No.79/2023 be set aside.

4. In support of the contention, counsel for the petitioner placed reliance on the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Nemi Chand and another Vs. Edward Mills Company Limited and another [(1952) 2 SCC 409].

entities.text: Nemi Chand and another Vs. Edward Mills Company Limited and another [(1952) 2 SCC 409]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, counsel for the respondent opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection while affirming the impugned order passed by the First Appellate Court.

6. Both the parties are heard at length and perused the documents filed NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:21956 3 MP-941-2024 by them.

7. From perusal of the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court, it appears that although the defendant/petitioner has deposited the arrears of rent before the Trial Court during pendency of the civil suit and counsel for the petitioner submits that he has not challenged the judgment passed by the Trial Court in respect of arrears of rent, but from perusal of the appeal memo, it appears that appellant/petitioner has filed the civil appeal for seeking quashment of judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court, therefore, the contention made by counsel for the petitioner cannot be accepted.
Petitioner/defendant challenged the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court on all the grounds.
8. Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Ismail Khan Vs. Shankarlal Chaurasia [1984 JLJ 609]

entities.text: Ismail Khan Vs. Shankarlal Chaurasia [1984 JLJ 609]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: has held that "cross-objection preferred under Explanation to Order 41 Rule 22(1) of CPC is to be treated as an application and Court fee has to be paid accordingly and not ad-valorem Court fee under Article 1 of Schedule 1 of the Court-fee Act.

9. Section 8 of the Court Fee Act, 1870 provides as under:-
"8. Fee on memorandum of appeal against order relating to compensation.--The amount of fee payable under this Act on a memorandum of appeal against an order relating to compensation under any Act for the time being in force for the acquisition of land for public purposes, shall be computed according to the difference between the amount awarded and the amount claimed by the appellant."
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:21956 4 MP-941-2024 Smt Divya Shrivastava vs Baijnath Prasad on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104930264/
2 10. Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner has not paid Court fee as valued by the plaintiff/respondent in the original civil suit.
Hence, First Appellate Court has rightly directed the petitioner/defendant to pay the deficit Court fee of Rs.30,720/-.
There is no illegality or perversity in the impugned order passed by the First Appellate Court and this petition deserves to be dismissed.
11. Accordingly, this miscellaneous petition devoid of merits and substance and is hereby dismissed.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Abhi Smt Divya Shrivastava vs Baijnath Prasad on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104930264/
